It broke working unit tests and so did it break Foundation Sites and possibly more (and the migrations for the deprecations are not documented so far if we need any). =(
I did a `git bisect` and the mentioned commit was the cause.

We don't have time to sift through someone else's test suite. The instructions in our new issue template are quite clear:
>  Briefly describe the issue you've encountered
>  *  What do you expect to happen?
>  *  What actually happens?
>  *  Which browsers are affected?
>  Provide a *minimal* test case, see https://webkit.org/test-case-reduction/

@ncoden what do you think? So far jQuery 3.3 breaks 40 unit tests and so does it Foundation Sites.
@DanielRuf have you verified that this change actually fixes Zurb? Also is the second commit here the correct one? It still has a `console.log` in it so I'm wondering if the changes were intended.

Yes, it fixes Zurb Foundation Sites. I cloned jQuery into node_modules/jquery, did `git bisect` and always created a fresh build.

I have force pushed a new commit but it is not here because the PR is already closed.
At least https://github.com/chaijs/chai-jquery is affected too and possibly much more. The change clearly introduced a breaking change regarding the behavior compared against 3.2.1.

This was supposed to be a bug fix, which is why it was not held to a semver major. The fact that the unit tests have to be reversed tells me that there is some assumption made somewhere (jQuery or Zurb) that isn't correct.  To the point @gibson042 made, we could really use a reduced test case. I looked at the failing Zurb tests and can't quite work through them. I'm out of time for now. I will note, however, that Zurb is using ES classes compiled through Babel which may be introducing some strange behavior.

You can easily verify it by cloning foundation-sites, installing the dependencies, going into the node_modules directory, deleting the jquery directory and recreating it with a git clone. In there do a `git checkout https://github.com/jquery/jquery/commit/a16339b8933f115da3661f3d3f64854c3fa60bdc`, rebuild and rerun the testsuite of foundation-sites.

My first check was to compare the dep trees of a succeeding and a failing commit and the difference was jQuery 3.2.1 vs 3.3.1. I checked all commits with `git bisect` in the jquery directory which clearly gave https://github.com/jquery/jquery/commit/a16339b8933f115da3661f3d3f64854c3fa60bdc as cause.

I'll provide some more commands from the Travis CI build.

issue_context.body: https://github.com/jquery/jquery/commit/a16339b8933f115da3661f3d3f64854c3fa60bdc introduced a bug. The typecheck is not correct. The `toType` method was not used and produces failing unit tests at https://github.com/zurb/foundation-sites
comments: Please provide a link to a reduced test case demonstrating your issue.
Basically the failing unit tests at https://github.com/zurb/foundation-sites/commits/develop

A link to unit tests a test case is not. We need something reduced to demonstrate a clear issue in isFunction. There's a lot going on in those tests and one of the failures follows a codepath that never touches jQuery. And how `getAttribute` being undefined on a supposed script tag led you to `isFunction` is entirely unclear.
BTW, https://jsfiddle.net or https://jsbin.com or good places to start.

Well, `git bisect` showed this exact commit and change as I already wrote ;-) (and I always compiled jQuery for each `git bisect` iteration)

I'll try to create a reduced testcase when I find the time for it this week.

> `git bisect` showed this exact commit and change as I already wrote

Not to be mean, but this doesn't help us at all. We have to require a test case or we'd be forced to sift through everyone's applications. Ain't nobody got time for that.
> I'll try to create a reduced testcase when I find the time for it this week.

It was supposed to be an answer to
> And how getAttribute being undefined on a supposed script tag led you to isFunction is entirely unclear.

> It was supposed to be an answer

I see what you mean now. git bisect led you there. Fair enough, but what's still unclear is how the two are related. Thank you for when you get to the test case. We'll be happy to take a closer look then.

Generally I also miss the changes for https://github.com/jquery/jquery-migrate as this is a big breaking change here.

I am currently revisitng this issue and trying to fix some parts in foundation-sites but it's still confusing that the one mentioned code part affects `elem.getAttribute( "type" )`.

Also imo a deprecation is still not directly a change in the code part but only a warning on the console that a deprecated feature is used.

Here it was one step too much I think. Never saw other solutions introducing deprecations which broke production code but just threw warnings (especially when it comes to node modules).

Or do you see it different?

Most of the time it is also a change in the code. We move deprecated APIs to the `deprecated` module which can be excluded in a custom build.

Deprecation is unrelated to this issue, though. We still need a test case.
cc @ncoden I guess this is the issue. Not sure if another testrunner or testframework or headless browser testing framework would be a solution but many still use mochajs and phantomjs.

Thank you so much for finally providing a test case. The issue is in your [mocha-phantomjs](https://github.com/nathanboktae/mocha-phantomjs) dependency, which itself depends upon an ancient version of phantomjs ([1.9.7-15](https://github.com/nathanboktae/mocha-phantomjs/blob/master/package.json#L42) instead of the [latest 2.1.7](https://www.npmjs.com/package/phantomjs)). That version suffers from a bug in which NodeList objects are functions, thus causing `jQuery.map` to iterate over them as objects rather than as arrays (with the catastrophic results you observe).

For proof, run the following invocations (or `npx`-free equivalents) in the root directory of your [mocha-jquery-test](https://github.com/DanielRuf/mocha-jquery-test) repository:
* `echo 'console.log("typeof NodeList: " + typeof document.getElementsByTagName("*"))' | npx phantomjs`
* `echo 'console.log("typeof NodeList: " + typeof document.getElementsByTagName("*"))' | npx phantomjs@2.1.7`

We don't support ancient versions of phantomjs, so the correct fix is to get that dependency updated in mocha-phantomjs.

Understandable but I see no big reason for this change as the internal check was the only thing that has changed in the commit.

In this case it should be documented that 3.3.x+ does not support phantomjs 1.x anymore (not sure why this is not caught like in the other parts where jQuery has fixes for phantomjs and some specific browsers).

At this point I'm no longer sure what you're asking for. The `isFunction` behavior change was necessary to fix #3596 and #3600, as [I've already explained](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/pull/3956#discussion_r164288713)—how could we know when a function is _really_ a NodeList? And environments that we fully support are listed at http://jquery.com/browser-support/ , although we could add a note describing [best-effort support for others](https://github.com/jquery/jquery/blob/7eec97aab3476ea0094766dec958e2a0372feac3/Gruntfile.js#L122-L125) ([PRs welcome](https://github.com/jquery/jquery.com/blob/master/pages/browser-support.html)).

review_comments: These changes are incorrect, function-mimicking objects are not callable and object-mimicking functions still are (and `jQuery.isFunction` is intended to test that characteristic).
Well, but it didn't and a simple `typeof` told otherwise.

Right, the failure was reported in #3600 and fixed in a16339b8933f115da3661f3d3f64854c3fa60bdc, and we still don't know why you want to revert that because you haven't provided a reduced test case demonstrating your unfulfilled expectations.

This change is incorrect, `fn` is supposed to be a generator or async function in browsers that support those constructs. We just use `Function` to avoid syntax errors in the test suite itself for browsers that don't support them.
I ran the testsuite locally and this caused also a failing unit test on your side.
The "deprecated" module is passing in all browsers: http://swarm.jquery.org/job/6744
This change is incorrect, a `then` method that mimics another type must still be used because that's how native Promises behave.
Sure, but the unit test awaits a thenable, not an empty string.
Right, it needs to await a thenable _in which the `then` method mimics a non-function_.
I'm confused. Shouldn't a function-mimicking object return `false` when tested against `jQuery.isFunction()` (and `true` for object-mimicking function)? Why the change here?
obj is changed to Function a few lines above and typeof gives function for this. And also the new isFunction check. The literal sets it to another type.

My PR is just a partly fix as the unit tests sre not correct and the expected behaviour of the new method in general after its deprecation (still do not know what is needed to migrate other things and plugins which rely on these. Personally I hoped there would have been a beta release instead of rushing out with a new one and without testing against big frameworks).

@DanielRuf it's always possible to test against master. As you can imagine there are a LOT of major frameworks using jQuery and we can't take on the responsibility of testing every release against them. Does Zurb have its CI set up to test against jQuery betas? If so a beta would have caught this. If not, I don't think it would have made a difference.
See package.json. Just (stable) releases are installed by npm.
This change is incorrect; a function that mimics another type must still be invoked by `.then` because that's how native Promises behave.

Well, the test was also failing here as you can see on Travis when using the right definition for the deprecated functions. A deprecation should not change the behavior of its previous method definition.
The deprecation didn't change anything, the fix for #3596 did. And the entire "deferred" module is passing tests just fine: http://swarm.jquery.org/job/6744
